report.source_text: Under a light microscope, 19 glomeruli could be identified and all these glomeruli appeared normal. Tubular epithelial cells were distended by abundant, large, cytoplasmic vacuoles, while the blood vessels were normal (Figure 1B). The interstitial inflammation was accompanied by interstitial edema and focal interstitial infiltration with eosinophils and lymphocytes (Figure 1C). These findings were consistent with interstitial nephritis.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 42-year-old man sustained massive Asian giant hornet envenomation with 66 sting marks, presenting with oliguria (200 ml/24h), leukocytosis, and sinus bradycardia. Initial workup on day 3 revealed acute kidney injury (serum creatinine 185 μmol/L) coexisting with severe rhabdomyolysis (CK 5342 U/L), elevated transaminases, and cardiac injury (troponin I 1.092 ng/ml, CK-MB 577 U/L). Despite normalization of cardiac markers by approximately day 13, renal function progressively deteriorated (creatinine rising to 534 μmol/L with persistent oliguria). Renal biopsy performed on day 17 demonstrated normal glomeruli, tubular epithelial vacuolization, and interstitial edema with focal infiltration by eosinophils and lymphocytes, establishing the diagnosis of interstitial nephritis. The patient was treated with methylprednisolone 32 mg/day, resulting in clinical improvement by day 31 with increased urine output (>2.8 L/day) and decreasing creatinine (159.3 μmol/L).
